coverage_summary: The Stage 1 scGPT autoregressive path is largely supported, including pseudo-bulk averaging, opaque BioFM encoding, projection, tokenization, lookup, soft-token injection, and teacher-forced training. The record omits documented alternative training, lifecycle, modality, evaluation, and text-preparation paths, and overstates a separate target embedding table.

findings.detail: The trajectory covers only AR alignment, while the paper documents an alternative CT alignment mode that bypasses the LLM forward pass and uses bidirectional InfoNCE.

evidence.quote: Alternatively, to avoid the costly forward pass required by a large LLM, [...] we evaluate an alternative alignment mode. In this variant, we use contrastive learning to directly align the bio embeddings with their paired text embeddings.

we also study a contrastive alignment mode that enforces representation-level similarity. Here, the projected bio embeddings [...] are aligned with text embeddings [...] using a bidirectional InfoNCE loss

findings.required_change: Add a separate Stage 1 CT trajectory with its paired text-embedding target and bidirectional InfoNCE boundary, or explicitly mark CT as outside the record scope.

findings.detail: The record stops after Stage 1 and omits the documented Stage 2 instruction-tuning lifecycle, including the trainable LoRA path and templated prompts.

evidence.quote: In the subsequent instruction-tuning stage, we allow both Pθ and the low-rank adapter (LORA) within the LLM to be trainable.
For Stage 2 instruction tuning, we augment the alignment dataset with templated prompts paired to the biological-text examples.

findings.required_change: Add a Stage 2 instruction-tuning trajectory/phase with prompt augmentation, projected biological tokens, LLM input, and the documented LoRA trainability state.

findings.detail: The assembly represents only scGPT with Granite-3.3-8B-Instruct, omitting documented BioFM variants and the direct general-domain LLM encoder route, as well as protein and molecule evaluation paths.

evidence.quote: We evaluate representative foundation models across three modalities [...] scGPT [...] ESM-2 [...] and ChemBERTa [...]. We also include MAMMAL [...]. Finally, we consider a general-domain LLM used directly as a bio encoder.
We evaluate all four protein-oriented text generation benchmarks from Mol-Instructions
The molecular description generation task in Mol-Instructions [...] evaluates a model's ability to produce detailed free-text descriptions of molecules

findings.required_change: Add trajectories for the documented encoder/model variants and downstream modality tasks, or state that this record intentionally covers only the scRNA-seq Stage 1 route.

findings.detail: The CellxGene preparation step omits the documented textual-description branch. The target_text node is introduced later without provenance from cell/tissue metadata or the described language-model generation process.

evidence.quote: pseudo-bulk RNA samples are generated by averaging single-cell profiles, and natural-language descriptions are produced from cell and tissue metadata using large language models.

findings.required_change: Add the metadata-to-natural-language-description branch as an opaque documented boundary, or connect target_text to an explicitly external paired-description source and preserve this provenance.

findings.detail: The AR text branch is modeled with a separate target_embedding_table whose identity and lookup path are not established. The paper states that AR consumes Tokens(t_b), while its four alternative pooled language representations concern the contrastive target ϕ(t_b).

evidence.quote: When performing alignment training using AR loss, the model consumes Tokens(t_b) directly, since the objective is next-token prediction over a text sequence.
We evaluate four ways to construct ϕ(t): (1) TokEmbed [...] (2) LL-Mean [...] (3) LayerAvg [...] and (4) LLM-Embed

findings.required_change: Represent AR target-token consumption as an opaque teacher-forcing input or bind it to the same documented LLM input-embedding resource; remove the unsupported separate target-specific table unless the source establishes it.
